clue.text: Plate of inedible toasted aphid hearts

indicators.note: the hearts of the three words are their central letters, taken from each in turn

explanation.surface: A plate served with toasted aphid hearts, which nobody could eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate and a dish are both flat vessels for serving food, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Image caught inside hospital

indicators.note: inside says the letter for caught sits within the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital for convalescents
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A picture captured in a hospital, perhaps an X-ray or ultrasound.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical image produced by a scanner is itself called by this name, a noun sense.

clue.text: Rude, popular and very fast

parts.note: IN means fashionable or popular
SO means very, as in 'so good'
LENT is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Describes someone as rude, popular and very quick, an odd mix of qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but it is a noun: Lent, the forty-day fast before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent behaviour is disrespectful and cheeky, a close synonym for impolite or rude.

clue.text: Something outstandingly good Lieutenant found in drink

indicators.note: found in places the abbreviation for the officer within the word for drink

parts.note: BEER is a drink

explanation.surface: An excellent find: a lieutenant discovered in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a cracking song, goal or performance is called by this informal noun meaning a superb example.

clue.text: Drops reserve at parties

parts.note: SUB is a substitute or reserve player
SIDES are parties in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A reserve player gets dropped from the team at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' reads as a verb about leaving out a player, but it means falls or abates.
explanation.definitionFit: Floodwater or a fever that lessens or sinks back is said to fall, an intransitive verb sense.

clue.text: During tango performance is unimpaired

parts.note: IN means during, as in 'in the summer'
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ACT is a performance

explanation.surface: A dancer's tango performance comes off without a hitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undamaged is untouched, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Uniformed fiend concealing rage on rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
concealing means the fiend's letters wrap around the word for rage

parts.note: a DEVIL is a fiend
IRE is rage

explanation.surface: A demon in uniform hides a growing fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rise' is a down-clue reversal: the whole fiend-around-rage string is read upward, giving DEIREVIL turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants wearing livery, a distinctive household uniform, are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Bachelor lounged around club

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Bachelor, as in BA

indicators.note: around here means the letters of lounged are moved about

explanation.surface: A single man idles about the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a social venue, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy short stick used as a weapon is a cudgel, the noun sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Trivial study in order to follow inner mind

indicators.note: to follow puts the study and order pieces after the inner letters
inner takes the central letters of the word mind

parts.note: CON means to study or learn by heart
SEQUENTIAL means in order, one after another

explanation.surface: Dismisses a psychological study as trivial in its probing of the inner mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' means the study and order pieces come after the inner letters, even though the clue names them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no importance or consequence is petty, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Worker dropping dead with joint complaint and chill

indicators.note: dropping says the abbreviation for dead is removed from the worker

parts.note: a HAND is a manual worker, as in farmhand
GOUT is an inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: An exhausted worker, laid up with gout and a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chill' poses as a cold, but it is the slang verb for relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax casually, often with friends, is in slang to loaf about; both are idiomatic verbs.

clue.text: Missile taking tip off part of bone

indicators.note: taking tip off removes the first letter of the word for part of bone

parts.note: MARROW is the soft tissue inside bone

explanation.surface: A missile that knocks the tip off a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft fired from a bow is a projectile, so the archer's missile fits.

clue.text: Algae offspring holds in wonder

indicators.note: holds means the offspring word contains the wonder word

parts.note: SEED means offspring, as in biblical 'his seed'
AWE is wonder

explanation.surface: A child, staring at pond scum, is held in wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp and wrack are marine algae, the collective plant life of the shore.

clue.text: Quietly consult socialist that's more highly valued

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
REFER means consult, as in refer to a dictionary
RED is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A discreet consultation with a socialist whose opinion counts for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chosen over others is favoured, valued above alternatives.

clue.text: Commonplace section of last rites

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Remarks that a part of the last rites is routine and ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase overused until stale is banal, which is what commonplace means.

clue.text: Second go to secure love

parts.note: WEE is informal for urinate, as in 'go' to the toilet
TIE means to secure or fasten

explanation.surface: A second attempt to win someone's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' looks like an attempt; here it is the childish verb for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate terms of address for a dear one, like darling.

clue.text: Shellfish brand found in concessions

indicators.note: found in puts the brand word inside the concessions word

parts.note: SOPS are concessions made to placate someone
to CALL means to brand or label, as in branding someone a traitor

explanation.surface: A seafood label turns up among discounted items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand' looks like a trademark noun, but it is the verb to label.
explanation.definitionFit: Bivalve molluscs with ridged fan-shaped shells are an example of edible shellfish.

clue.text: Challenging dramatic performance by divorcee

parts.note: an EX is a former spouse
ACTING is dramatic performance

explanation.surface: A divorced partner gives a demanding, theatrical display.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is demanding of skill or effort is difficult, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Journalist with a yen to cover up — exceedingly common

indicators.note: to cover up means the outer letters wrap around the word for exceedingly

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist
VERY means exceedingly
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A journalist with a yearning to hush something up, which is all too usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' poses as a longing but gives Y; ED, A and Y surround VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary and routine, found daily, is common in the ordinary sense.

clue.text: Deputy of diminished reputation

indicators.note: diminished means the last letter is cut from the word for reputation

parts.note: STANDING is status or reputation

explanation.surface: A deputy whose reputation has suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who takes another's place temporarily is a deputy, both nouns.

clue.text: Worker with one day to get unknown element

parts.note: an ANT is a worker, as in worker ant
I is the Roman numeral one
MON is the abbreviation for Monday
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A worker spends a day finding an unknown chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: This metalloid with symbol Sb is an example of a chemical element.

clue.text: Produce offspring

definitions.meaning: to put out or publish, as in releasing a stamp or statement

explanation.surface: Instruction to have children.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to release or put out; the noun is a legal word for one's descendants.

clue.text: Modify commercial apartment

parts.note: an AD is a commercial

explanation.surface: Change an advert for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something to suit new conditions is to adjust it, a synonym.

clue.text: Large plant leaves whispered in concord

indicators.note: whispered signals that the pieces are spoken, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: a TREE is a large plant; TEA is the dried leaves of the tea plant

explanation.surface: A large plant's leaves rustle softly in harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departure; it is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between nations is an accord or concord.

clue.text: Identify with English shipmate at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of shipmate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feel for an English sailor on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To share and understand another's feelings is to relate to them, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Cake made by mean relative

parts.note: PAR is the average or mean, as in below par
KIN means a relative

explanation.surface: A cake baked by a stingy relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' suggests stingy but gives PAR, the norm. Parkin is a sticky oat and treacle gingerbread from northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshire gingerbread made with oatmeal and treacle is an example of cake.

clue.text: Draw large aquatic mammal at head of Yangtze

parts.note: an OTTER is an aquatic mammal

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of Yangtze

explanation.surface: Sketch a big otter at the source of China's great river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb to sketch; it is the noun, a prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle where winners are picked by chance is a draw, noun to noun.

clue.text: Hiker, artist, doctor and queen crossing line

indicators.note: crossing means the group of pieces lies across the line letter, holding it

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A hiker, a painter, a doctor and a queen walk across a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who walks for pleasure in the countryside is a walker or hiker.

clue.text: Head of the French after Christ's arrival

indicators.note: after puts the letters for Christ's arrival behind the French article

parts.note: LE is French for the
AD, Anno Domini, dates from Christ's birth

explanation.surface: A French leader comes after the birth of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in front or in charge is to head, as in heading a march.

clue.text: Philanderer about to embrace a king

indicators.note: to embrace has the word for about holding the next pieces

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A womaniser is set to hug a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissolute man given to womanising is a libertine or rake.

clue.text: US period when a puritan monk cut loose?

indicators.note: cut loose means set free, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks what period in American history saw a puritan monk freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period' suggests an era; in American usage it is the full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a full stop a period, which is one example of a piece of punctuation.
